title: Degree is additive on tensor products of invertible modules on proper schemes of dimension at most one
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. With tensor product as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and degree $\deg_k(\mathcal F)=\chi(X,\mathcal F)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for an invertible module as in [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], one has $\deg_k(\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal M)=\deg_k(\mathcal L)+\deg_k(\mathcal M)$.

proof.text: We first check the coherence hypothesis that will be used on each component. For any proper $k$-scheme $Y$, its structure map is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The field $k$ is Noetherian: every ideal containing a nonzero element contains $1$ and is the whole ring; the zero ideal is generated by $0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The one-point affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has its whole space as an affine Noetherian cover and is quasi-compact [def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] implies that $Y$ is Noetherian. An invertible module on $Y$ is quasi-coherent and locally generated by one element [def-sc-invertible-module], so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes it coherent. This applies both to $X$ and to every proper integral component below.

source.place: Tag 0AYX, hypotheses for the reduction; Properties Tag 01OV and Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XZ

proof.text:
The product $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], applied with $f=\mathrm{id}_X$. Apply [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components] to the three invertible modules $\mathcal L$, $\mathcal M$, and $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M$ on $X$. It supplies the same finite list of proper integral dimension-one schemes $C_i$ and the same finite weights $m_i$, determined by $X$, with
$$\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\sum_i m_i\deg_k(\mathcal L|_{C_i}),\quad \deg_k(\mathcal M)=\sum_i m_i\deg_k(\mathcal M|_{C_i}),\quad \deg_k(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=\sum_i m_i\deg_k((\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)|_{C_i}).$$
No contribution from an isolated zero-dimensional component or an embedded point is added: the cited formula already concerns all of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0AYX, first sentence of proof; Tag 0AYW; invertibility of the tensor product by Modules Tag 01CT (via lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor)

proof.text: Fix $i$ and put $L_i=\mathcal L|_{C_i}=j_i^*\mathcal L$ and $M_i=\mathcal M|_{C_i}=j_i^*\mathcal M$ for the closed immersion $j_i:C_i\to X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] with $f=j_i$ shows that both are invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], and $M_i$ is coherent by Step 1. At the generic point its fibre is one-dimensional, so its generic rank is $1$. The hypotheses of [lem-trf-curve-euler-tensor-generic-rank] hold by Step 2, and that formula with $\mathcal L=L_i$, $\mathcal F=M_i$ gives $\chi(C_i,L_i\otimes M_i)=\deg_k(L_i)+\chi(C_i,M_i)$. Subtracting $\chi(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$ and using [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] yields $\deg_k(L_i\otimes M_i)=\deg_k(L_i)+\deg_k(M_i)$. The tensor whose degree occurs in Step 2 identifies with this tensor: clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] with $f=j_i$ gives an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{C_i}$-modules $(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)|_{C_i}=j_i^*(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)\cong j_i^*\mathcal L\otimes j_i^*\mathcal M=L_i\otimes M_i$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; no flatness of $j_i$ is needed. Euler characteristics and hence degrees are unchanged by isomorphism, since the induced maps on every cohomology group are inverse [def-pc-euler-characteristic].

source.place: Tag 0AYX, second sentence of proof; Tag 0AYV with n=r=1; restriction/tensor isomorphism by Modules Tags 01CD and 01CT (via lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor)

proof.text:
Substitute the component identity of Step 3 into the third sum in Step 2 and distribute the finite sum:
$$\deg_k(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=\sum_i m_i(\deg_k(L_i)+\deg_k(M_i))=\sum_i m_i\deg_k(L_i)+\sum_i m_i\deg_k(M_i)=\deg_k(\mathcal L)+\deg_k(\mathcal M).$$
All equalities are in $\mathbf Z$. If there are no dimension-one components, the three sums are empty and all three degrees are zero, so the same calculation applies, including $X=\varnothing$.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the 0B5X proof this is the tensor-product degree formula used to pass from the degree of a positive tensor power to the degree of the line bundle and to obtain linear Euler-characteristic growth.
